stages.name: Economic growth and government finances
stages.title: Economic growth and government finances
stages.sub: How growth changes what the government collects and what it must spend.

steps.q: Unemployment is falling and more people are in jobs earning wages. Each of those wages gets taxed. What happens to the amount of income tax collected?
steps.hint: More people earning wages means more wages being taxed.

steps.q: With fewer people out of work, how many people need to claim unemployment benefits?
steps.hint: Benefits are paid to people without jobs. If more people have jobs, what happens to that number?

steps.q: Tax collected is rising and benefit payments are falling at the same time. What does this do to the government's finances?
steps.wrong: It makes no difference to them
steps.hint: More money coming in and less money going out.
steps.pre: This is the government revenue benefit of growth:

steps.q: As the economy grows, more people commute, more goods are transported, and more housing is needed. What is likely to happen to roads, transport and housing in a growing economy?
steps.right: They become stretched and need expanding
steps.wrong: They easily cope without any changes
steps.hint: More output and more people usually mean more pressure on what already exists.

steps.q: To keep up with a growing, congested economy, the government has to build new roads, railways and housing, and write new rules to manage it all. Does this cost the government anything?
steps.right: Yes, it has to spend more money
steps.wrong: No, this happens without any government spending
steps.hint: Building infrastructure and writing regulation both require resources and money.
